name: Barclays Global Investors

summary.text: Barclays Global Investors (BGI) was the asset-management business of Barclays PLC, including the iShares exchange-traded fund platform. In April 2009 Barclays agreed to sell iShares alone to CVC Capital Partners for about $4.4 billion; after unsolicited interest in the whole business, Barclays accepted a binding offer from BlackRock on June 12, 2009 for approximately $13.5 billion in cash and BlackRock shares, paid CVC a $175 million termination fee, and completed the sale on December 1, 2009, when the consideration was valued at $15.2 billion and Barclays took a 19.9% economic interest in the enlarged BlackRock. Barclays presented the sale as adding to its Core Tier 1 capital ratio. BlackRock's 10-K attributes $1.850 trillion of assets under management to the BGI acquisition.

facts.claim: On April 9, 2009 Barclays announced the sale of its iShares business to CVC Capital Partners for a total consideration of approximately $4.4 billion. Barclays subsequently received unsolicited interest in the whole of BGI and entered discussions with BlackRock, which culminated in the June 12, 2009 announcement of a binding offer. On June 16, 2009 CVC and Barclays agreed to terminate the iShares Master Sale Agreement and Barclays agreed to pay CVC a termination fee of US$175 million (£108 million), after which Barclays entered into the agreement with BlackRock for the sale of BGI.
facts.quote: the sale of its iShares business ("iShares") to CVC Capital Partners SICAV-FIS S.A. ("CVC") for a total consideration of approximately $4.4billion on 9 April 2009 / On 16 June 2009, CVC and Barclays agreed to terminate the iShares Master Sale Agreement and Barclays agreed to pay CVC the agreed termination fee of US$175 million (£108 million) in aggregate, following which Barclays entered into an agreement with BlackRock for the sale of BGI.

facts.claim: On June 12, 2009 Barclays announced a binding offer from BlackRock for the Barclays Global Investors business for consideration of approximately US$13.5 billion (£8.2 billion): US$6.6 billion (£4.0 billion) in cash and about US$6.9 billion (£4.2 billion) in 37.784 million new BlackRock shares, valued at BlackRock's June 11, 2009 closing price, giving Barclays an economic interest of approximately 19.9% of the enlarged BlackRock group.
facts.quote: The consideration would be approximately US$13.5 billion (£8.2 billion) of which US$6.6 billion (£4.0 billion) would be received in cash and approximately US$6.9 billion (£4.2 billion) in shares based on the closing price of BlackRock's common stock on 11 June 2009. / Barclays would receive 37.784 million new BlackRock shares giving it an economic interest of approximately 19.9% of the enlarged BlackRock Group.

sources.title: Barclays PLC Form 6-K: binding offer from BlackRock for Barclays Global Investors

facts.claim: Barclays presented the BGI sale in capital terms: in June 2009 it estimated the gain would add about 163 basis points to Equity Tier 1 and 150 basis points to Core Tier 1 capital ratios as at December 31, 2008; its first-half 2009 results gave pro forma Core Tier 1 of 8.8% and Tier 1 of 11.7% assuming the sale; and at completion it estimated the transaction would have added about 185 basis points to Core Tier 1 and 124 basis points to Tier 1 as at June 30, 2009.
facts.quote: This gain would add an estimated 163bps to Equity Tier 1 and 150bps to Core Tier 1 capital ratios as at 31 December 2008. / This transaction would have added an estimated 185bps to Core Tier 1 and 124bps to Tier 1 capital ratios as at 30 June 2009.

facts.claim: Barclays shareholders approved the sale of BGI to BlackRock at a general meeting on August 6, 2009. The sale completed on December 1, 2009; Barclays reported the consideration at completion as US$15.2 billion (£9.5 billion), including 37.567 million new BlackRock shares giving Barclays an economic interest of 19.9% of the enlarged BlackRock group.
facts.quote: The consideration at completion was US$15.2 billion (£9.5 billion), including 37.567 million new BlackRock shares giving Barclays an economic interest of 19.9% of the enlarged BlackRock group. / On 6th August 2009 shareholders approved BlackRock's offer to purchase the Barclays Global Investors business

facts.claim: BlackRock's 10-K for 2009 states that the BGI acquisition added $1.850 trillion of assets under management, taking BlackRock from $1.307 trillion at December 31, 2008 to $3.346 trillion at December 31, 2009.
facts.quote: At December 31, 2009, BlackRock managed $3.346 trillion of AUM, a 156%, or $2.039 trillion, increase relative to BlackRock's reported AUM at December 31, 2008.

facts.claim: In May 2012 Barclays stated that it intended to sell its entire remaining holding in BlackRock through a secondary offering and a buyback, with BlackRock repurchasing up to $1.0 billion of its stock from Barclays.
facts.quote: intended to sell its entire holding via the offering and buyback, with BlackRock repurchasing up to $1.0 billion of its stock from Barclays

openQuestions: The CVC passages ('9 April 2009 ... approximately $4.4billion', 'On 16 June 2009, CVC and Barclays agreed to terminate...') came from Barclays' SEC filings in the search results, but the search did not say which filing holds each sentence; the 2009 6-K exhibit (u07193exv1.htm, which reads like the shareholder circular) and the 2009 20-F are cited. Confirm with check-links.mjs and a read of each.
The first-half 2009 'Core Tier 1 at 8.8% and Tier 1 at 11.7% pro forma' passage is attributed to the August 3, 2009 interim-results 6-K on the basis of its date; confirm.

No retrieved source describes the price as low or high relative to BGI's value; the brief's 'pennies on the dollar' is not supported by any source found. The sources record a $13.5 billion offer (US$15.2 billion at completion) for a business that added $1.850 trillion of AUM, and Barclays booking a gain that raised its Core Tier 1 ratio.
BGI's pre-sale AUM and a description of BGI's history (for example, Wells Fargo Nikko Investment Advisors origins) were not retrieved; Britannica's BGI entry appeared in results without a passage.
